s: interest lending is forbidden toward Israelites (toward a brother, any kind of interest)
q: You shall not lend on interest to your brother: interest of money, interest of food, interest of anything that is lent on interest.

s: interest lending is permitted toward foreigner
q: You may charge a foreigner interest;

s: vows must be paid the LORD your God (the LORD will surely require it; delay is sin)
q: When you vow a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not be slack to pay it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you; and it would be sin in you.

s: vows is optional Israelites (refraining from a vow is no sin)
q: But if you refrain from making a vow, it shall be no sin in you.

s: neighbor's vineyard and grain prohibits using a sickle (on standing grain)
q: When you come into your neighbor’s standing grain, then you may pluck the ears with your hand; but you shall not use a sickle on your neighbor’s standing grain.

s: Ammonite is excluded from the LORD's assembly (even to the tenth generation, forever)
q: An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the LORD’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall no one belonging to them enter into the LORD’s assembly forever,

s: Moabite is excluded from the LORD's assembly (even to the tenth generation, forever)
q: An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the LORD’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall no one belonging to them enter into the LORD’s assembly forever,

s: Ammonite failed to provide bread and water (to Israelites on the way out of Egypt)
q: because they didn’t meet you with bread and with water on the way when you came out of Egypt

s: Moabite hired Balaam (to curse the Israelites)
q: because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you.

s: divorce requires certificate of divorce (written by the husband and put in the wife's hand)
q: he shall write her a certificate of divorce, put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.

s: hired servant is owed wages on the same day (before sunset)
q: In his day you shall give him his wages, neither shall the sun go down on it, for he is poor and sets his heart on it

s: foreigner is entitled to justice (may not be deprived of it)
q: You shall not deprive the foreigner or the fatherless of justice, nor take a widow’s clothing in pledge;

s: fatherless is entitled to justice (may not be deprived of it)
q: You shall not deprive the foreigner or the fatherless of justice, nor take a widow’s clothing in pledge;

s: widow is protected from clothing taken in pledge
q: nor take a widow’s clothing in pledge;

s: gleaning harvest (sheaf, olives, vineyard) is reserved for foreigner (forgotten sheaf, olive boughs, vineyard gleanings)
q: It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

s: gleaning harvest (sheaf, olives, vineyard) is reserved for fatherless (forgotten sheaf, olive boughs, vineyard gleanings)
q: It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

s: gleaning harvest (sheaf, olives, vineyard) is reserved for widow (forgotten sheaf, olive boughs, vineyard gleanings)
q: It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

s: the LORD your God regards as abomination remarriage of former husband to divorced wife (after she has been defiled)
q: for that would be an abomination to the LORD.

s: the LORD your God gives inheritance land
q: You shall not cause the land to sin, which the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance.

s: pledge may not include mill (taking the mill or upper millstone is forbidden because it takes a life in pledge)
q: No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge, for he takes a life in pledge.

s: lender may not enter neighbor's house (to get the pledge)
q: When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.

s: neighbor (the borrower) brings pledge to lender (outside the house)
q: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge outside to you.

s: pledge must be restored by sunset (when the borrower is poor, so he may sleep in his garment)
q: You shall surely restore to him the pledge when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his garment and bless you.

s: lender may not sleep with pledge (when the borrower is a poor man)
q: If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge.

s: hired servant has status poor and needy (may be a brother or a foreigner within the gates)
q: You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the foreigners who are in your land within your gates.

s: levirate marriage requires surviving brother (when a brother dies without a son)
q: Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.

s: honest weights and measures requires perfect and just weight and measure (commanded of Israel)
q: You shall have a perfect and just weight. You shall have a perfect and just measure

s: honest weights and measures results in long days in the land (promised outcome)
q: that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

s: the LORD your God regards as abomination those who act unrighteously
q: all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to the LORD your God.

s: the LORD your God gives Canaan (as inheritance to Israel)
q: in the land which the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance to possess it

s: Amalek attacked Israel (struck the feeble rearmost on the way out of Egypt)
q: how he met you by the way, and struck the rearmost of you, all who were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary

s: Amalek lacks fear of God
q: he didn’t fear God.

s: Amalek is destined for blotting out of memory (commanded of Israel once at rest)
q: you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.

s: levirate marriage has purpose preserving dead brother's name (firstborn succeeds in his name)
q: It shall be that the firstborn whom she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother who is dead, that his name not be blotted out of Israel.

s: firstborn son succeeds dead brother (in his name)
q: the firstborn whom she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother who is dead

s: widow is forbidden to marry stranger (when husband dies without a son)
q: the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger.

s: dead brother has status childless
q: one of them dies and has no son

s: widow is wife of dead brother
q: the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger.

s: surviving brother is brother of dead brother (husband's brother of the widow)
q: Her husband’s brother shall go in to her

s: sandal removal ritual is performed by widow (when surviving brother refuses levirate marriage)
q: then his brother’s wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and loose his sandal from off his foot, and spit in his face.

s: sandal removal ritual is performed on surviving brother (as shaming for refusing duty)
q: So shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother’s house.

s: surviving brother is named The house of him who had his sandal removed (after refusing and undergoing the ritual)
q: His name shall be called in Israel, “The house of him who had his sandal removed.”

s: the LORD your God gives Canaan (as an inheritance to the Israelites)
q: when you have come in to the land which the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance

s: first fruits offering consists of first of the fruit of the ground (brought in a basket)
q: you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground, which you shall bring in from your land that the LORD your God gives you. You shall put it in a basket

s: first fruits offering is presented at place the LORD shall choose
q: shall go to the place which the LORD your God shall choose to cause his name to dwell there.

s: first fruits offering is set before altar of the LORD (placed there by the priest)
q: The priest shall take the basket out of your hand, and set it down before the LORD your God’s altar.

s: priest receives first fruits offering (takes the basket from the worshiper)
q: The priest shall take the basket out of your hand

s: tithe of the third year is given to Levites (also foreigner, fatherless, widow)
q: then you shall give it to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, that they may eat within your gates and be filled.

s: tithe of the third year occurs in third year (the year of tithing)
q: in the third year, which is the year of tithing

s: Egypt was lived in by Israel's ancestor, few in number (he went down into Egypt)
q: He went down into Egypt, and lived there, few in number.

s: the LORD your God swore to give land to fathers
q: I have come to the land which the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.

s: Canaan is described as land flowing with milk and honey
q: has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

s: the LORD your God brought out of egypt Israelites (with a mighty hand and outstretched arm)
q: The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand, with an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs, and with wonders;

s: the LORD your God hears Israelites (heard their cry in affliction)
q: The LORD heard our voice, and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.

s: the LORD your God dwells in heaven (holy habitation)
q: Look down from your holy habitation, from heaven

s: the LORD your God commands statutes and ordinances (to be kept with all heart and soul)
q: Today the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances.

s: the LORD your God declares as possession Israelites (a people for his own possession)
q: The LORD has declared today that you are a people for his own possession, as he has promised you

s: the LORD your God will make high Israelites (above all nations, in praise, name and honor)
q: He will make you high above all nations that he has made, in praise, in name, and in honor

s: Moses commands Israel (together with the elders of Israel)
q: Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, “Keep all the commandment which I command you today.

s: plastered stones (stones inscribed with the law) is located at Mount Ebal (to be set up after crossing the Jordan)
q: you shall set up these stones, which I command you today, on Mount Ebal

s: altar (altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal) is located at Mount Ebal
q: on Mount Ebal, and you shall coat them with plaster. 5 There you shall build an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones.

s: altar (altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal) is made of uncut stones (no iron tool used)
q: You shall build the LORD your God’s altar of uncut stones.

s: altar (altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal) is dedicated to the LORD your God
q: There you shall build an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones.

s: altar (altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal) is used for burnt offerings
q: You shall offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.

s: Mount Gerizim hosts blessing (tribes stand there to bless the people)
q: These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people

s: Mount Gerizim is stood on by Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin (tribes assigned to bless)
q: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.

s: Mount Ebal hosts curses (tribes stand there for the curse)
q: These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

s: Mount Ebal is stood on by Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali (tribes assigned to the curse)
q: These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

s: Levites declares curses (say them with a loud voice to all the men of Israel)
q: With a loud voice, the Levites shall say to all the men of Israel,

s: Israel is a people of the LORD (became so on the day of Moses' address)
q: Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.

s: curses is answered with Amen (by all the people)
q: All the people shall answer and say, ‘Amen.’

s: curses applies to he who does not uphold the law by doing it (final curse)
q: ‘Cursed is he who doesn’t uphold the words of this law by doing them.’

s: curses protects foreigner, fatherless, and widow (against withheld justice)
q: ‘Cursed is he who withholds justice from the foreigner, fatherless, and widow.’

s: curses prohibits idol making (secretly setting up an engraved or molten image)
q: ‘Cursed is the man who makes an engraved or molten image, an abomination to the LORD, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and sets it up in secret.’

s: Israel has god the LORD your God
q: Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.

s: the LORD your God gives land (to Israel)
q: the land which the LORD your God gives you

s: the LORD your God is a God of the fathers of Israel
q: as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you.

s: land is described as flowing with milk and honey
q: a land flowing with milk and honey

s: land is located across Jordan (reached by crossing the Jordan)
q: you shall pass over the Jordan to the land which the LORD your God gives you

s: plastered stones (stones inscribed with the law) is coated with plaster
q: that you shall set yourself up great stones, and coat them with plaster.

s: plastered stones (stones inscribed with the law) is inscribed with law (all the words, very plainly)
q: You shall write on the stones all the words of this law very plainly.”

s: the LORD your God is god of Israel (covenant God)
q: the LORD your God

s: blessing and curse are conditioned on listening to the LORD's voice (obedience)
q: All these blessings will come upon you, and overtake you, if you listen to the LORD your God’s voice.

s: curses are conditioned on not listening to the LORD's voice (disobedience)
q: if you will not listen to the LORD your God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command you today, that all these curses will come on you and overtake you.

s: curses serve as sign and wonder (to Israelites and offspring forever)
q: They will be for a sign and for a wonder to you and to your offspring forever.

s: commandments, statutes, and ordinances are given by Moses (commanded today)
q: the commandments of the LORD your God which I command you today

s: distant nation has language not understood by Israelites
q: a nation whose language you will not understand,

s: distant nation has disposition fierce, no respect for elderly or young
q: a nation of fierce facial expressions, that doesn’t respect the elderly, nor show favor to the young.

s: distant nation originates from end of the earth
q: from far away, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies

s: Egypt is source of diseases of Egypt (boils and diseases feared by Israelites)
q: He will bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt, which you were afraid of; and they will cling to you.

s: Egypt is destination of Israel (returned by ships as slaves)
q: The LORD will bring you into Egypt again with ships

s: exile and scattering among nations has effect no rest and trembling heart (among the nations)
q: Among these nations you will find no ease, and there will be no rest for the sole of your foot; but the LORD will give you there a trembling heart, failing of eyes, and pining of soul.

s: the LORD your God establishes Israel (as a holy people to himself, conditional on keeping commandments)
q: The LORD will establish you for a holy people to himself, as he has sworn to you, if you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and walk in his ways.

s: exile and scattering among nations extends from one end of the earth to the other (scattering by the LORD)
q: The LORD will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth.

s: the LORD your God gives Canaan (to the Israelites)
q: He will bless you in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

s: the LORD your God swore to give land to fathers
q: in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.

s: the LORD your God brings against israelites distant nation (as punishment for disobedience)
q: The LORD will bring a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies

s: Israel is called by name of the LORD your God (seen by all peoples of the earth)
q: All the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by the LORD’s name, and they will be afraid of you.

s: Israel receives commandments from Moses (commanded today)
q: all his commandments which I command you today

s: Israel will possess Canaan (going in to possess it)
q: from off the land where you go in to possess it.

s: Israel was formerly numerous as the stars of the sky (multitude)
q: even though you were as the stars of the sky for multitude

s: the LORD your God commands Moses (to make the covenant in Moab)
q: These are the words of the covenant which the LORD commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab

s: Israel has ancestor Jacob (fathers of Israel)
q: as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

s: Israel lacks a heart to know, eyes to see, ears to hear (as of the time of speaking)
q: But the LORD has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.

s: Israel experienced wilderness wanderings (forty years, clothes and sandals did not wear out)
q: I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes have not grown old on you, and your sandals have not grown old on your feet.

s: Israel witnessed Egyptian plagues and wonders
q: Your eyes have seen all that the LORD did in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;

s: Israel defeated Sihon (king of Heshbon)
q: Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we struck them.

s: Israel defeated Og (king of Bashan)
q: Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we struck them.

s: Israel gave land as inheritance to Reubenites (land taken from Sihon and Og)
q: We took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.

s: Israel gave land as inheritance to Gadites (land taken from Sihon and Og)
q: We took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.

s: Israel gave land as inheritance to Manassites (half-tribe; land taken from Sihon and Og)
q: We took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.

s: Israel includes foreigners (in Israel's camps) (cutters of wood and drawers of water)
q: and the foreigners who are in the middle of your camps, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,

s: covenant of Moab is a covenant in addition to the Horeb covenant
q: in addition to the covenant which he made with them in Horeb.

s: idolatrous individual (among Israel) is a person whose heart turns from the LORD to serve other gods (man, woman, family, or tribe)
q: lest there should be among you man, woman, family, or tribe whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations;

s: idolatrous individual (among Israel) believes he will have peace despite stubbornness (blesses himself on hearing the curse)
q: “I shall have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,”

s: the LORD your God will not pardon idolatrous individual (among Israel)
q: The LORD will not pardon him, but then the LORD’s anger and his jealousy will smoke against that man

s: idolatrous individual (among Israel) is subject to curses of the covenant (name blotted out)
q: all the curse that is written in this book will fall on him, and the LORD will blot out his name from under the sky.

s: curses of the covenant is written in commandments, statutes, and ordinances (book of the law)
q: according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.

s: devastated land has condition sulfur, salt, and burning; unsown, unproductive
q: that all of its land is sulfur, salt, and burning, that it is not sown, doesn’t produce, nor does any grass grow in it

s: devastated land is compared to Sodom (overthrown by the LORD in anger)
q: like the overthrow of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath.

s: the LORD your God overthrew Sodom (in anger and wrath)
q: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath.

s: the LORD your God overthrew Gomorrah (in anger and wrath)
q: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath.

s: the LORD your God overthrew Admah (in anger and wrath)
q: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath.

s: covenant of Moab made with Israel (including children, wives, foreigners, and future generations)
q: These are the words of the covenant which the LORD commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab

s: the LORD your God overthrew Zeboiim (in anger and wrath)
q: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath.

s: devastated land was devastated because abandoning the covenant and serving other gods (explanation given by men)
q: Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt,

s: the LORD your God uprooted Israel (thrust into another land in anger)
q: The LORD rooted them out of their land in anger, in wrath, and in great indignation, and thrust them into another land, as it is today.”

s: the LORD your God owns secret and revealed things (secret things belong to the LORD; revealed things belong to us and our children)
q: The secret things belong to the LORD our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever

s: covenant of Moab located in Moab
q: in the land of Moab

s: covenant of Moab establishes Israel (as the LORD's people)
q: that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God

s: the LORD your God is god of Israel
q: that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, as he spoke to you and as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

s: the LORD your God swore to Abraham (to be God to his descendants)
q: as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

s: Israel has ancestor Abraham (fathers of Israel)
q: as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

s: Israel has ancestor Isaac (fathers of Israel)
q: as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

s: Esau's descendants (children of Esau) dwells in Mount Seir
q: the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir

s: Moab calls Emim (Moabites' name for the Rephaim)
q: but the Moabites call them Emim.

s: Sihon is a Amorite (king of Heshbon)
q: Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land

s: Sihon rules Heshbon (king)
q: Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land

s: Mount Seir given to Esau's descendants (children of Esau) (as a possession by the LORD)
q: because I have given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession.

s: Sihon refused Israel (would not let Israel pass; LORD hardened his spirit)
q: But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him, for the LORD your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate

s: battle at Jahaz has outcome Israel victory over Sihon (LORD delivered Sihon up)
q: The LORD our God delivered him up before us; and we struck him, his sons, and all his people.

s: battle at Jahaz is fought between Sihon (Sihon and his people came out against Israel)
q: Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz.

s: the LORD your God has relationship to Israel (God of Israel; has been with them forty years and they lacked nothing)
q: These forty years, the LORD your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing.

s: the LORD your God destroyed them (before Israel; Israel succeeded them and lived in their place)
q: but the LORD destroyed them from before Israel, and they succeeded them, and lived in their place,

s: Esau's descendants (children of Esau) is related to Israel (brothers)
q: You are to pass through the border of your brothers, the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir

s: Esau's descendants (children of Esau) succeeded Horites (destroyed them and lived in their place in Seir)
q: The Horites also lived in Seir in the past, but the children of Esau succeeded them.

s: Moab has land Ar (Ar is the border of Moab)
q: You are to pass over Ar, the border of Moab, today.

s: Moab is related to Lot's descendants (children of Lot) (Moab's land given to children of Lot)
q: for I will not give you any of his land for a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession.

s: Ammonites given to Lot's descendants (children of Lot) (land of Ammon given as a possession by the LORD)
q: for I will not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession, because I have given it to the children of Lot for a possession.

s: Ammonites calls Zamzummim (Ammonites' name for the Rephaim who lived there)
q: Rephaim lived there in the past, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

s: the LORD your God gathers Israelites (from all the peoples where he scattered them)
q: the LORD your God will release you from captivity, have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.

s: exile and scattering among nations has condition return and obedience (with all heart and soul)
q: and return to the LORD your God and obey his voice according to all that I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,

s: the LORD your God brings into promised land (the land their fathers possessed)
q: The LORD your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you will possess it.

s: the LORD your God performs circumcision of the heart (on the Israelites and their offspring, to love him)
q: The LORD your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your offspring, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live.

s: the LORD your God puts curses on enemies (on those who hate and persecuted Israel)
q: The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.

s: the LORD your God is life of Israelites (he is their life and the length of their days)
q: for he is your life, and the length of your days

s: the LORD your God swore land to fathers (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob)
q: the land which the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.

s: blessing and curse is set before Israelites (by Moses)
q: the blessing and the curse, which I have set before you

s: life and death choice has witness heaven and earth (called to witness against Israelites)
q: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse.

s: exile and scattering among nations involves scattering among nations (the LORD drove the Israelites there)
q: among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you

s: Moses has age 120 years (at time of speaking)
q: I am one hundred twenty years old today.

s: the LORD your God has covenant with Israel
q: will forsake me and break my covenant which I have made with them.

s: the LORD your God swore to give promised land (sworn to Israel's fathers)
q: the land which the LORD has sworn to their fathers to give them

s: the LORD your God destroyed Sihon (precedent for destroying the nations)
q: The LORD will do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.

s: the LORD your God destroyed Og (precedent for destroying the nations)
q: The LORD will do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.

s: the LORD your God will destroy nations of the land (before Israel)
q: He will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them.

s: Israel is predicted to worship other gods (after entering the land, forsaking the LORD)
q: This people will rise up and play the prostitute after the strange gods of the land where they go to be among them

s: Israel is described as rebellious (stiff-necked, stated by Moses)
q: For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck.

s: Israel will inherit promised land (sworn to their fathers)
q: you shall go with this people into the land which the LORD has sworn to their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.

s: Israel has set time end of every seven years, year of release, feast of booths
q: At the end of every seven years, in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of booths,

s: Moses is forbidden to cross Jordan (decree of the LORD)
q: The LORD has said to me, ‘You shall not go over this Jordan.’

s: Moses authored law (wrote it in a book)
q: Moses wrote this law and delivered it to the priests the sons of Levi

s: Moses authored song (wrote and taught it the same day)
q: So Moses wrote this song the same day, and taught it to the children of Israel.

s: Moses will die soon (stated by the LORD)
q: Behold, your days approach that you must die.

s: Joshua is successor of Moses (commissioned to lead Israel)
q: He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun, and said, “Be strong and courageous; for you shall bring the children of Israel into the land which I swore to them. I will be with you.”

s: Joshua will lead Israel (over the Jordan into the land)

q: But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked.

s: Moses is companion of Joshua (recited the song together)

s: Moses is brother of Aaron
q: as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor

s: Moses recites Song of Moses (to all Israel)
q: Moses finished reciting all these words to all Israel.

q: They sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods that they didn’t know, to new gods that came up recently, which your fathers didn’t dread.

q: Vengeance is mine, and recompense, at the time when their foot slides,

q: I will hide my face from them. I will see what their end will be;

q: For the LORD’s portion is his people. Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.

s: the LORD your God is father of Israel (made and established them)
q: Isn’t he your father who has bought you? He has made you and established you.

s: the LORD your God has attribute only god (no god with him)
q: See now that I myself am he. There is no god with me.

s: the LORD your God has power over life and death (kills and makes alive, wounds and heals)
q: I kill and I make alive. I wound and I heal. There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.

s: Israel is a people of the LORD
q: For the LORD’s portion is his people.

s: Israel has attribute perverse generation (corrupt, unfaithful)
q: They are a perverse and crooked generation.

s: Israel has attribute void of counsel (lacking understanding)
q: For they are a nation void of counsel. There is no understanding in them.

s: Moses is a man of God
q: Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death

s: the LORD your God saves Israel (a people saved by the LORD)
q: Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help, the sword of your excellency?

s: Israel dwells safety (in a land of grain and new wine)
q: Israel dwells in safety, the fountain of Jacob alone, In a land of grain and new wine.

s: Israel has enemies enemies (will submit and be trodden on)
q: Your enemies will submit themselves to you. You will tread on their high places.

s: Levi possesses Thummim and Urim (with his godly one)
q: Your Thummim and your Urim are with your godly one

s: Levi was proved at Massah
q: whom you proved at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah.

s: Levi teaches Jacob (ordinances)
q: They shall teach Jacob your ordinances, and Israel your law.

s: Levi keeps covenant (observes the word of the LORD)
q: for they have observed your word, and keep your covenant.

s: Levi offers incense (and whole burnt offering on the altar)
q: They shall put incense before you, and whole burnt offering on your altar.

s: Joseph has land blessed by the LORD your God
q: About Joseph he said, “His land is blessed by the LORD

s: Joseph was separated from his brothers
q: on the crown of the head of him who was separated from his brothers.

s: Moses commanded law (an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob)
q: Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.

q: They are the ten thousands of Ephraim.

s: Joseph has descendants Manasseh (the thousands of Manasseh)

q: This is the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death.

s: the LORD your God came from Sinai
q: The LORD came from Sinai, and rose from Seir to them.

s: the LORD your God shone from Mount Paran
q: He shone from Mount Paran.

s: the LORD your God loves Israel (the people)
q: Yes, he loves the people.

s: the LORD your God is unique among Jeshurun (no one like God)
q: There is no one like God, Jeshurun, who rides on the heavens for your help

s: the LORD your God is eternal God (dwelling place of Jeshurun)
q: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms.

s: Moses is a servant of the LORD
q: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the LORD’s word.

q: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him.

s: children of Israel obeys Joshua (listened and did as the LORD commanded Moses)
q: The children of Israel listened to him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.

s: Mount Nebo located opposite Jericho (Pisgah)
q: Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.

s: Moses' death and burial occurs in plains of Moab (land of Moab)
q: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the LORD’s word.

s: Moses' death and burial occurs according to the LORD your God (the LORD's word)
q: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the LORD’s word.

s: Moses' death and burial burial location valley opposite Beth Peor (tomb location unknown to this day)
q: He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth Peor, but no man knows where his tomb is to this day.

s: Moses age at death 120 years
q: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died.

s: Moses has attribute undimmed eyesight (at death)
q: His eye was not dim, nor his strength gone.

s: Moses has attribute undiminished strength (at death)
q: His eye was not dim, nor his strength gone.

q: Since then, there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

q: Since then, there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

s: Moses laid hands on Joshua (conferred the spirit of wisdom)
q: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him.

s: Moses was denied entry to land (only allowed to see it)
q: I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there.”

s: Moses performed signs and wonders in Egypt (sent by the LORD)
q: in all the signs and the wonders which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,

q: Og the king of Bashan came out against us

s: Bashan is also called land of Rephaim
q: (The same is called the land of Rephaim.

q: called them, even Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth Jair, to this day.)

q: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

q: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.

q: Og the king of Bashan came out against us

q: half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites;

q: half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites;

q: the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh

q: even to the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;
